name: Vaimoornathar Temple, Tiruvaimur
deity: Shiva as Vaimoornathar (Vaaimoornaathar, a swayambhu lingam), with the goddess Paalin Nanmozhiyal (Ksheeropa Vasani)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tiruvaimur, near Tirukkuvalai in the lower Kaveri delta, honours Shiva as Vaimoornathar — worshipped in a self-manifest lingam — with the goddess Paalin Nanmozhiyal. One of the Paadal Petra Sthalams on the southern bank of the Kaveri, it is remembered as the place bound to Sundarar, and counted the 124th shrine of the southern bank.

sections.history: Tiruvaimur, near Tirukkuvalai in the lower Kaveri delta, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned in the Tevaram, counted as the 124th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri. Set among the seven delta villages of this tract, it is tied in tradition to Sundarar, and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later. (Wikipedia places it in Tiruvarur district, the TN Temples Project in Nagapattinam; the two districts meet nearby.)
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Vaimoornathar — Vaaimoornaathar — worshipped in a swayambhu, self-manifest lingam, with the goddess Paalin Nanmozhiyal (Ksheeropa Vasani) in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The compact gopuram and walled courtyard are typical of the smaller Tevaram shrines of this southern tract.
sections.legends: The lord is a swayambhu, self-manifest, worshipped as Vaimoornathar; the goddess is praised as Paalin Nanmozhiyal, 'she of words sweet as milk,' and as Ksheeropa Vasani. The place is bound in Shaiva memory to Sundarar, among the delta shrines he hymned on the southern bank. As with many smaller delta temples, the fuller sthala purana survives chiefly in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a delta village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail of the southern Kaveri include Tiruvaimur among their stops near Tirukkuvalai.
sections.experience: At Tiruvaimur the pilgrim comes to a quiet shrine of the self-manifest lord. Before Vaimoornathar and Paalin Nanmozhiyal, in the green delta country near Tirukkuvalai, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the southern Kaveri, firm in the lingam that rose of itself and in the memory of the saint who sang here.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruvaimur lies near Tirukkuvalai, off the Nagapattinam–Tiruthuraipoondi road in the lower delta. Tiruthuraipoondi (about 8 km) and Tirukkuvalai are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Nagapattinam and Tiruvarur are the nearest rail heads.
